recorded.prompt:q-clock:a: Read the page and each keyed question. For every wrong option, say whether a passage of the page rules it out, and quote or name that passage.
recorded.pass:q-clock:a: an independent reader (18-happens-before q3), never the author
recorded.outcome:q-clock:a: ruled out: "The Difference Between Happens-before and Wall-clock Time" section: "Happens-before is about visibility, not real-time ordering... It does NOT mean W physically occurred before R on the clock." Clock ordering is explicitly not what decides visibility.
recorded.prompt:q-clock:c: Read the page and each keyed question. For every wrong option, say whether a passage of the page rules it out, and quote or name that passage.
recorded.pass:q-clock:c: an independent reader (18-happens-before q3), never the author
recorded.outcome:q-clock:c: ruled out: Pitfall #1's BrokenFlag example has the reader loop (`while (!ready) ;`) with the comment "might loop forever due to caching" / data prints "might print 0!" — looping to keep reading does not by itself guarantee the write is seen without a happens-before edge.
recorded.prompt:q-holder:a: Read the page and each keyed question. For every wrong option, say whether a passage of the page rules it out, and quote or name that passage.
recorded.pass:q-holder:a: an independent reader (18-happens-before q3), never the author
recorded.outcome:q-holder:a: ruled out: The Holder code declares 'static final SingletonIODH INSTANCE = new SingletonIODH();' (not volatile), and Edge Case #4 attributes the safety to 'A class's static initializer... happens-before the first access to any static field or method of that class', not to a volatile read.
recorded.prompt:q-holder:b: Read the page and each keyed question. For every wrong option, say whether a passage of the page rules it out, and quote or name that passage.
recorded.pass:q-holder:b: an independent reader (18-happens-before q3), never the author
recorded.outcome:q-holder:b: ruled out: 'The Initialization-on-Demand Holder (IODH) idiom exploits this guarantee to create a thread-safe, lazily initialized singleton without any synchronized blocks in the getInstance() method' and the code comment 'No synchronization needed — guaranteed thread-safe by JMM' — there is no locking/serialization mechanism, so plain 'static' cannot be what makes calls run one at a time.
